# Vacuum-salt plant, vapour recompression evaporator: data sheet

REAL DESIGN DATA from US Patent 5,366,514 (Texas Brine Corp., 1994), FIG. I and Table I: a 2,500 short-ton-per-day
plant making 99.99 % NaCl from solution-mined brine. The P&ID was drawn by PlantAgent on that flowsheet (tags, line
numbers, valves and relief settings are ours). Equipment ratings marked ILLUSTRATIVE are not in the patent.

## Operating point (patent Table I, converted to SI)
| Stream / item | Value |
|---|---|
| Feed brine to E-101 (line 1001), saturated NaCl (~26 wt %) | 362.9 t/h at 24 °C |
| Brine leaving E-101 | 60 °C |
| Elutriating brine to the evaporator legs | 98.0 t/h at 60 °C |
| Brine through E-102 to V-201 (lines 1003/1004) | 264.9 t/h, 60 → 125.6 °C |
| V-201 VRC evaporator | 1.70 bar(a) (10 psig), brine boiling at 125.6 °C |
| V-201 overhead to K-201 (line 3001) | 226.8 t/h steam, saturation 115.2 °C at 1.70 bar(a) |
| K-201 discharge | 3.08 bar(a) (30 psig), pressure ratio 1.8 |
| Steam to E-201 after D-201 (line 3003), incl. 15.9 t/h turbine exhaust | 251.7 t/h at 135 °C, 3.08 bar(a) |
| E-201 condensate (line 4001) | 251.7 t/h at 134.4 °C, cooled in E-102 to about 82 °C |
| Excess V-201 vapour to E-301 (line 3101) | 20.9 t/h |
| Purge liquor V-201 → V-301 (line 5001) | 47.6 t/h at 125.6 °C |
| V-301 purge evaporator | about 1.01 bar(a), 108.9 °C |
| Purge to disposal well (line 5101) | 6.8 t/h at 108.9 °C |
| Purge-evaporator overheads to E-101 (line 3201) | 25.4 t/h at 100.6 °C after desuperheating |
| Salt produced (dry) | 94.9 t/h (2,511 short t/d) |

## What the patent says about the equipment
- K-201 is a single-wheel centrifugal compressor, 1.8:1, driven by a gas turbine. "The VRC compressor can only pass a
  fixed amount of steam": the vapour above its suction capacity (about 90 % of the boil-up passes it) is the excess sent
  to the purge evaporator heater E-301 (patent col. 7-8).
- Desuperheating condensate is sprayed into the compressor discharge (D-201) because superheated steam transfers heat
  poorly in the large circulating heaters (col. 7).

## Equipment ratings
- K-201 suction capacity: 226.8 t/h (the patent's fixed compressor throughput). Shaft power: not stated in the patent.
- E-201 circulating heater: 8,800 m², U 2,000 W/m²K in service (ILLUSTRATIVE; 2,500 W/m²K clean).
- P-201 forced-circulation pump: 15,000 m³/h rated (ILLUSTRATIVE).
- E-301 purge-evaporator heater: 900 m² (ILLUSTRATIVE).
- Relief: PSV-201 on V-201 set 3.5 barg, PSV-202 on D-201 set 4.5 barg, PSV-301 on V-301 set 1.0 barg (ours).

## Process requirements and design rules
- Brine temperature rise through E-201 at most 3 K: a larger rise flashes in the tubes and scales them with salt.
- Condensate leaves E-201 saturated at the shell pressure.
- The brine boils above the steam saturation temperature by its boiling point elevation (use the brine_bpe tool).

## Modelling scope (from the plant's process engineer)
- The capacity question is decided by the VRC loop: V-201 boil-up, K-201, D-201 and the circulating heater E-201, plus the
  purge evaporator V-301 with E-301 that takes the excess vapour. Model that loop in detail.
- The feed preheat train (P-101, E-101, E-102) is not in question: take the brine entering V-201 from Table I (264.9 t/h
  at 125.6 °C, plus 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 °C, both scaling with throughput) instead of closing the
  condensate-to-brine heat-recovery loops.
- Turbine exhaust steam joining the compressor discharge: 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a), fixed (the gas turbine does not
  grow with salt production).

## Request
Sales wants the plant to make **3,000 short tons per day instead of 2,500 (+20 %)**.

REAL DESIGN DATA from US Patent 5,366,514 (Texas Brine Corp., 1994), FIG. I and Table I: a 2,500 short-ton-per-day
plant making 99.99 % NaCl from solution-mined brine. The P&ID was drawn by PlantAgent on that flowsheet (tags, line
numbers, valves and relief settings are ours). Equipment ratings marked ILLUSTRATIVE are not in the patent.

## Operating point (patent Table I, converted to SI)
| Stream / item | Value |
|---|---|
| Feed brine to E-101 (line 1001), saturated NaCl (~26 wt %) | 362.9 t/h at 24 °C |
| Brine leaving E-101 | 60 °C |
| Elutriating brine to the evaporator legs | 98.0 t/h at 60 °C |
| Brine through E-102 to V-201 (lines 1003/1004) | 264.9 t/h, 60 → 125.6 °C |
| V-201 VRC evaporator | 1.70 bar(a) (10 psig), brine boiling at 125.6 °C |
| V-201 overhead to K-201 (line 3001) | 226.8 t/h steam, saturation 115.2 °C at 1.70 bar(a) |
| K-201 discharge | 3.08 bar(a) (30 psig), pressure ratio 1.8 |
| Steam to E-201 after D-201 (line 3003), incl. 15.9 t/h turbine exhaust | 251.7 t/h at 135 °C, 3.08 bar(a) |
| E-201 condensate (line 4001) | 251.7 t/h at 134.4 °C, cooled in E-102 to about 82 °C |
| Excess V-201 vapour to E-301 (line 3101) | 20.9 t/h |
| Purge liquor V-201 → V-301 (line 5001) | 47.6 t/h at 125.6 °C |
| V-301 purge evaporator | about 1.01 bar(a), 108.9 °C |
| Purge to disposal well (line 5101) | 6.8 t/h at 108.9 °C |
| Purge-evaporator overheads to E-101 (line 3201) | 25.4 t/h at 100.6 °C after desuperheating |
| Salt produced (dry) | 94.9 t/h (2,511 short t/d) |

## What the patent says about the equipment
- K-201 is a single-wheel centrifugal compressor, 1.8:1, driven by a gas turbine. "The VRC compressor can only pass a
  fixed amount of steam": the vapour above its suction capacity (about 90 % of the boil-up passes it) is the excess sent
  to the purge evaporator heater E-301 (patent col. 7-8).
- Desuperheating condensate is sprayed into the compressor discharge (D-201) because superheated steam transfers heat
  poorly in the large circulating heaters (col. 7).

## Equipment ratings
- K-201 suction capacity: 226.8 t/h (the patent's fixed compressor throughput). Shaft power: not stated in the patent.
- E-201 circulating heater: 8,800 m², U 2,000 W/m²K in service (ILLUSTRATIVE; 2,500 W/m²K clean).
- P-201 forced-circulation pump: 15,000 m³/h rated (ILLUSTRATIVE).
- E-301 purge-evaporator heater: 900 m² (ILLUSTRATIVE).
- Relief: PSV-201 on V-201 set 3.5 barg, PSV-202 on D-201 set 4.5 barg, PSV-301 on V-301 set 1.0 barg (ours).

## Process requirements and design rules
- Brine temperature rise through E-201 at most 3 K: a larger rise flashes in the tubes and scales them with salt.
- Condensate leaves E-201 saturated at the shell pressure.
- The brine boils above the steam saturation temperature by its boiling point elevation (use the brine_bpe tool).

## Modelling scope (from the plant's process engineer)
- The capacity question is decided by the VRC loop: V-201 boil-up, K-201, D-201 and the circulating heater E-201, plus the
  purge evaporator V-301 with E-301 that takes the excess vapour. Model that loop in detail.
- The feed preheat train (P-101, E-101, E-102) is not in question: take the brine entering V-201 from Table I (264.9 t/h
  at 125.6 °C, plus 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 °C, both scaling with throughput) instead of closing the
  condensate-to-brine heat-recovery loops.
- Turbine exhaust steam joining the compressor discharge: 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a), fixed (the gas turbine does not
  grow with salt production).

## Request
Sales wants the plant to make **3,000 short tons per day instead of 2,500 (+20 %)**.

submit.label: vrc_cal_v2_desup_hx
assumptions: Brine modelled as Water with Steam Tables (IAPWS-IF97) package; saturated crystallising brine in V-201 and V-301 handled by evaporator with x_NaCl omitted, so salt_kg_h and boiling-point elevation are reported by the unit. brine_bpe at 1.70 bar: water 115.17 C, saturated brine 124.86 C, BPE 9.69 K; at 1.01 bar: brine 108.68 C, BPE 8.72 K.
CONFLICT used site data: E-201 installed area 8,800 m2 from data sheet Equipment ratings row (U 2,000 W/m2K in service) over P&ID E-201 DesignHeatTransferArea 6,500 m2.

CONFLICT used site data: P-201 rated flow 15,000 m3/h from data sheet Equipment ratings row over P&ID P-201 DesignVolumeFlowRate 12,000 m3/h; this rating is entered as a limit check and the simulated circulation exceeds it - not hidden.

K-201 shaft-power limit 14,000 kW from P&ID K-201 DesignShaftPower; data sheet states shaft power is not stated in the patent. Suction capacity 226.8 t/h from data sheet Equipment ratings and Table I row for line 3001.

Feed preheat train P-101, E-101, E-102 and T-401 excluded per data sheet Modelling scope row: 'take the brine entering V-201 from Table I (264.9 t/h at 125.6 C, plus 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 C) instead of closing condensate-to-brine heat-recovery loops'. Their connections 1002,1003,4201,4002,4001,4101,3201 and 4301 are therefore boundary flows, not closed in the VRC model.

Turbine exhaust 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a) is fixed and does not scale with throughput, per data sheet Modelling scope row; its temperature is not stated, assumed 200 C superheated vapour as a feed - it only affects the D-201 mixer/desuperheating duty, D-201 outlet is fixed at the measured 135 C.

D-201 desuperheater modelled as a mixer for turbine exhaust followed by cooler unit D-201 fixed at 135 C (data sheet line 3003 row). The condensate spray itself is not recirculated as a material stream because E-201 condensate is produced downstream of D-201 in DWSIM sequence; spray is represented by the cooler duty. Hence simulated S3003/E-201 condensate mass is 242.7 t/h vs measured 251.7 t/h, the 9.0 t/h difference being the spray - stated in calibration.

V-201 forced-circulation loop 2001-2002-2003 modelled once-through: CIRC_S2001 feed at the measured brine temperature 125.6 C and 1.70 bar vessel pressure plus pump head, through P-201 (dP 1.33 bar, eff 80% assumed - no efficiency on P&ID/data sheet) and E-201 rating, returning as S2003. No recycle unit used because supply temperature is set by V-201 boiling, per instruction for known-temperature loops.

E-301 is the heating side of evaporator V-301 (heating stream S3101v to S4101, area 900 m2 from P&ID E-301 DesignHeatTransferArea and data sheet) plus, in topology terms, its cold circulation is the V-301 feed; a separate E-301 hx rating was probed separately and not sequenced in the final logged run due to DWSIM double-use of the heating stream - E-301 area check is therefore via V-301 area_needed vs 900 m2.
Compressor K-201 efficiency 75% assumed (not on P&ID or data sheet), discharge fixed at 3.08 bar(a) (data sheet K-201 discharge row, ratio 1.8 = P&ID DesignPressureRatio).

V-301 feed in the final run is taken at its measured body condition 108.9 C liquid (data sheet V-301 row / purge disposal row) via valve 5001/FV-301, because feeding 125.6 C vapour-fraction feed flashes in DWSIM and gives negative boil duty; purge mass 47.6 t/h, excess heating vapour 20.9 t/h and disposal 6.8 t/h are all preserved.

Relief valves 7001/PSV-201 (3.5 Bar, P&ID V-201), 7002/PSV-202 (4.5 Bar) and 7003/PSV-301 (1 Bar) carry no normal flow and are not modelled as process units; vessel pressure limits in the run use P&ID design pressures V-201 3.5 BarGauge and V-301 1 BarGauge converted to absolute (4.51 / 2.01 bar).

E-201 brine rise requirement at most 3 K (data sheet Process requirements row) entered as E-201 cold outlet limit 125.6+3.0=128.6 C; condensate leaves saturated at shell pressure entered as hot outlet 134.4 C (data sheet E-201 condensate row).
